- When sentiment is positive (≥0.27) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.23) and forecast is rising, slow the upward trend and add a downward correction of 2–5% in the next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply a 3–5% downward bias to first 7–10 days.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model often overreacts — cap forecast increases at 3–4% per day to avoid mean reversion lag.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to correct — adjust forecast to align with 2–3-day moving average of recent prices.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to overfit recent trends — use 3–5-day sentiment smoothing before forecasting.
